div.l: Of double worstede was his semy cope
That rounded was as a bell oute of presse
Som̄ what he lipsed for his wauntonesse
To make his englissh swete vpon his tonge
And in his harping whan he hadde songe
His eyen twynkeled in his hede a right
As don̄ þe sterres in þe frosti night
This worthi lymyture was called huberd
A Marchaunt þere was with a forked berde
In motle hie on horse he sate
Vpon his hede a Flaundres beuer hate
His botes clapsed feyre and fetisly
His resons he spak ful solempnely
Shewing alwey þe encrece of his wynnyng
He wold þe see were kept for any thing
Bitwene Middelborgh and Orwell
Wel couth he in eschaunge sheldes sell
This worthi man his wit ful wel be set
Ther wist no wight that he was in dette
So estatly was he in gouernaunce
With his bargayns and with his cheuesaunce
For soth he was a worthi man with all
But soth to say I not how men him call
A clerk there was of Oxenford also
That vnto logik had longer I go
As lene was his horse as a rake
And he was fat I vndertake
But luked holowe and therto soberly
Ful threde bare was his ouerest curtby
For he had not goten him yit no benefice
Nor he was not worthi to haue no office
For him was leuer to haue at his beddis hede
xx . bokes clodde in blak and in rede
Of Aristotle and of his philosophie
Than robes riche or fither and Sauterie
But al þat he was a philosophre
Yit had he litul gold in cofre
But al þat he might of his frendes haue hente
On bokes and on lernyng he it spente
And besely gan for þe saules pray
Of hem þat yaf to scole ay
Of study toke he moost cure and hede
No worde spak he more / þan was nede
